name: BlockForge
hook: A programmable voxel world engine where a script becomes a world, and a world becomes a film.
problem: World-building and short-form 3D media usually mean hand-placing content in heavy editors, with no clean way for code, agents or version control to drive the result.
built: Housam built BlockForge end to end (934 of 934 sampled commits are his, March to November 2026): a browser isometric/3D builder, a native C++17/SDL2 client, schema-based world and object descriptions, a shared Luau mod host compiled for native and WASM, and CLI/MCP interfaces that let an agent build, inspect and film scenes. He also built the public landing site, rendered entirely from the engine.
highlights: Browser and native C++17/SDL2 clients sharing world formats and a Luau mod host (native and WASM), with build settings aimed at cross-client floating-point determinism
Object compiler derives physics properties (mass, centre of mass, inertia, colliders) from compiled objects
World versioning with diff and merge, plus a world-history film generated from the version graph
CLI bridge and MCP server with query and snapshot observation, so agents can see what they build
Timeline and film tooling used to render several short films (One World, Baalbek, Atom to Bomb, Claymation and others)
Status notes reference roughly 1,040 passing tests (self-reported, not rerun)
